subject: ClearPath commercial packaging tradeoffs & term structure
messages:
From: Jared Cole <jared.cole@clearpath.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya@clearpath.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging options & early-exit economics for ClearPath

Karthik —

Thanks for the intro call last week. We're preparing an internal comparison between Redwood and our incumbent provider (InferStack) and I need a clearer picture of how you typically structure commercial packaging for customers with two main asks: 1) flexible seat vs usage tradeoffs (we have variable inference volume across product lines) and 2) what early-exit / migration credits you offer if we commit to a year and then need to move off during year 1.

High level context: we currently spend ~$480k ARR on inference + reserved instances; planned growth to ~750k over next 12 months. Key constraints are predictable unit cost, rollback path for regulatory pilots, and minimal ops friction during migration.

Can you share the options (commit tiers, seat vs per-token mixes, and any standard credit windows)? If you have a short matrix or banded examples that map to throughput tiers that would help the exec team.

We're looping legal for the credit language — copied above.

Thanks,
Jared
Jared Cole
Head of Product Ops | ClearPath AI
Attachments: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Cole <jared.cole@clearpath.ai>
Cc: Priya Raman <priya@clearpath.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options & early-exit economics for ClearPath

Jared —

Appreciate the context. I've attached a compact worksheet that outlines three commercial pathways we commonly propose for accounts with mixed steady + spiky usage:

1) Committed-usage (preferred for predictability) — monthly committed tokens with step-down credits if usage undershoots. Strongest unit price, minimal per-request throttling.

2) Seat + Variable (hybrid) — seat licenses for steady baseline throughput (dedicated concurrency) + pay-per-token for burst. Good for product orgs with stable inference per-seat and unpredictable spikes.

3) Short-term Dedicated Pool (sprint pilot) — reserved GPU pool for a bounded pilot (90–180 days) with a fixed onboarding credit; converts to commited-usage pricing after conversion.

For early-exit: our standard is a declining onboarding/exit credit tied to committed run-rate and timing of termination. Typical structure we show: 6-month full credit (onboarding support/one-time setup), then a 50% credit in months 7–9, and 25% months 10–12 — this is negotiable but aligns incentives around successful ramp. We rarely do full buyouts unless there's a strategic swap and higher ACV.

I've attached a mock term sheet and a pricing band workbook (RWF_ClearPath_Pricing_v1.xlsx) to make this concrete. Highlights:
- SLA: 99.9 for Dedicated; 99.5 for Hosted depending on commitment tier
- Data residency: options for region pinning on Dedicated/Private
- Ramp window: we assume a 90-day technical ramp to reach committed throughput; credits are front-loaded to cushion ops/workload migration.

Quick ask: can we schedule 30 minutes tomorrow to walk the bands with your procurement and legal? Connor (cc'd) will be on-hand for technical fit and transformation costs.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachments: RWF_ClearPath_Pricing_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), term-sheet-clearpath-0624.docx (draft term sheet)
From: Priya Raman <priya@clearpath.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Cole <jared.cole@clearpath.ai>, ClearPath Legal <legal@clearpath.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 10:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options & early-exit economics for ClearPath

Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turn and the workbook — we reviewed it internally. A couple of clarifying items before we set up time:

- On the seat + variable model, can you clarify how you size "seat" capacity? Is it concurrency-based (slots per seat) or an allocation of baseline tokens? We want a model that doesn't penalize us for short bursts across many users.

- Regarding the declining credit schedule: is that purely a one-time onboarding credit, or does it include partial compensation for unrecoverable migration engineering costs (e.g., rewiring pipelines, audit updates)? Our legal wants explicit language that credits can be applied to migration services or invoice credits.

- For pilots with dedicated pools, do you offer a migration playbook and a rollback clause if latency/regression thresholds are missed in the pilot? We're particularly cautious because some vendors we've trialed had materially different warm-cache behavior in production.

On the quote workbook, the 12–24 month committed tiers look attractive, but we need to understand if you have a middle ground — say a 9-month ramp with prorated credits — because our fiscal planning doesn't map cleanly to 12 mo.

"On Mon, 22 Jun 2026 at 11:08, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai> wrote:"
> For early-exit: our standard is a declining onboarding/exit credit tied to committed run-rate and timing of termination. Typical structure we show: 6-month full credit (onboarding support/one-time setup), then a 50% credit in months 7–9, and 25% months 10–12 — this is negotiable but aligns incentives around successful ramp.

Appreciate the transparency — looping legal for the credit language. Can Connor join the call to talk about runtime parity and cache-warm strategies?

Thanks,
Priya Raman
VP, Product | ClearPath AI
Attachments: none
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Packaging options & early-exit economics for ClearPath

Team —

Quick internal note and recommendation before the joint call:

- Commercial stance: offer a 9-month prorated onboarding credit (75% year-1 credit taper) for a signed 12-month commit at the mid-tier. This preserves runway for ClearPath while protecting Redwood from a full buyout scenario.

- Packaging recommendation: present the seat+variable hybrid as the default commercial path. It maps well to their mixed workloads and gives us a chance to upsell committed tokens once they hit predictable volume thresholds.

- Technical guardrails: Connor to prepare a short doc on cache-warm expectations and an observability checklist we will enforce during pilot (latency SLO smoke tests, KV cache-warm checklist, token-throughput baselining). Make sure the pilot term sheet includes an explicit rollback clause tied to the observability checklist.

Karthik — propose we offer the adjusted credit schedule in the draft term-sheet and mark the clause "migration credits applicable to professional services or invoice credit" for legal review. I'll join the call from revenue leadership side.

Laura Bennett
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
Attachments: none
